key_insight: RetroChessBench exposes persistent failures in rule-based chess-history reasoning despite strong frontier-model mathematical capabilities.
engineering_relevance: Rule-constrained reconstruction tasks can reveal reasoning weaknesses that familiar mathematical benchmarks may miss.
method: Introduce 12 retrograde-chess tasks spanning exact-length constructions, unique endings, and exhaustive answer sets.
Provide references, scoring rubrics, and a terminal-reward environment.
Evaluate GPT 6 Astra High twice per task, with and without code execution.
evidence_signal: Required final answers failed in 22/24 attempts without tools and 18/24 with code execution; mean terminal RL rewards were 14.75% and 27.19%, respectively.
watch_item: The small, single-model evaluation limits generalization, and the proposed link to scarce worked explanations in training data remains a hypothesis.
paper_title: RetroChessBench: A Benchmark for Reconstructing and Proving Chess Histories
